sub: Judgement, confession, no hedging. Someone's getting read.

1.name: Opening Shots
q: On three, both say how tonight is actually going out of ten.~Different numbers? The lower one explains. No diplomatic 7s.
Guess what I thought about you in the first ten seconds. I'll tell you how close you got.
Say the least flattering true thing you've noticed about me so far.~It has to be true. That's the only rule.
What's an opinion you hold that would make most people here think less of you?~Say it, then I rate how brave that actually was out of ten. Under five, go again.
Five seconds, first instinct: what am I bad at? Go.
Point at whichever of us is more likely to ruin this. Three, two, one — point.~Now defend it.
Guess the thing everyone agrees is good that I genuinely think is overrated.~Then we both say ours. Whoever's is more universally loved wins.
Which of us needs this more? Answer honestly, not politely.
Rate my confidence out of ten. Then tell me whether that was a compliment.
Guess what I assumed about you that I've already had to correct.~Then I tell you the real one, unedited.
Say the text you'd send your friend about me tonight. Word for word, out loud.
Five seconds, no thinking: what do I judge people for instantly? Go.~Then I tell you how close you got, and I refuse to feel bad about it.
Am I your type?~'Sort of' isn't an answer. Pick a side.
Who's trying harder right now — you or me? On three, both point.
What's the most annoying thing I've done since we sat down? Something small counts.
Name a compliment people give me that you think is a lie.~Then I tell you if you're right, and I take yours apart.
On three, both say something you believe that you've learned to stop saying out loud.~Same moment. You don't get to hear mine and pick a safer one.
Pick one and commit: I'm someone you'll remember, or someone you'll forget by Thursday.
Guess the pettiest reason I've ever written someone off completely.~You'll be too generous. Then I tell you the real one.
What's a red flag you've already clocked in me? There's at least one.~I don't get to defend myself until you've named it properly.
Which one of us is more full of it? Both answer at the same time.
On three, both say what you actually want from tonight. Real answers, not polite ones.~Different answers? The one who wants less explains first.
Guess the last lie I told and who got it. One shot.~Wrong? I tell you, and then you tell me yours.
Say the most arrogant true thing about yourself.~No hedging, no laughing it off at the end.
If you had to sabotage this in one sentence, what would you say?~Say it out loud in the tone you'd really use. I rate how well it would have worked.
Guess something I find attractive that I'm a bit embarrassed by.~Then I confirm or correct, and you owe me yours either way.
What have you already decided about me that you haven't said?~All of it. I stay quiet until you're done.
On three, both name a widely-loved thing you'd happily see wiped off the earth.~Then defend it against the other one for thirty seconds.
How much of what you've told me tonight has been performance? Out of ten.
Guess the question I'm hoping you don't ask.~Get it right and you have to ask it. Get it wrong and I have to tell you what it was.

2.name: No Take-Backs
q: On three, both rate the worst thing you've ever thought about someone you love, out of ten.~Higher number says the actual thought. You never have to name who.
What have you done that you'd be ashamed for me to know?~Give me a number out of ten first. Then I decide whether that number buys you out of saying it.
You can skip this card. But if you do, I get one question and you answer it properly.
Name someone you've been unfair to and never made right.~Then I rule out loud: real reason, or excuse. You don't get to argue the verdict.
Tell me the most selfish thing you've done that worked out perfectly.~Then I rate how guilty you actually seem, out of ten. Under five and you explain why not.
Argue for something you actually find indefensible. Thirty seconds. Make it good.
Say the meanest thing you've ever said to someone — word for word, in the tone you used.~Then I call it: did you mean it? You confirm or deny. No elaborating.
Guess who I secretly think I'm better than.~Then I get the same guess about you. Neither of us is allowed to say 'nobody'.
Five seconds, no thinking: name a rule you break constantly and won't stop. Go.~Then I decide whether that's a real rule or a soft one you picked to look good.
Guess my worst quality.~Right, and I owe you a real confession. Wrong, and you owe me one.
On three, both say something you want that you'd be judged for admitting.~Same moment. You don't get to hear mine first and adjust.
Name the last thing you did purely for how it would look.~Then I guess who you did it for. If I'm right, you tell me why their opinion still runs you.
Tell me about a time you were the villain.~Not the misunderstood version. The actual villain.
Guess what I lie about most often. One shot.~Wrong, I tell you the real one. Right or wrong, you still tell me yours.
Say something true about you that would make me walk.~Then I rule, out loud, on whether it actually would. You take the verdict.
Tell me the most manipulative thing you've done and got away with.~Then I decide whether you're proud of it. If I say you are, you don't deny it — you explain it.
Guess the compliment I fish for constantly. Then do an impression of how I fish for it.~I'll tell you how close both of those were.
On three, both name the thing you're secretly competing with your friends about.~Whoever's is pettier has to go into detail.
What are you most defensive about?~Now let me poke it.
Name one of my good qualities you think is mostly an act. Say it to my face.~Then I do the same to you, and neither of us gets to be hurt about it.
Name the thing you've never apologised for and never will. Then defend it like you're being accused.~Thirty seconds. I'm allowed to interrupt.
What would the person who likes you least say about you? Say it in their voice.
Say a thought you have regularly and never say out loud. Whisper it first.~Now say it again at normal volume. The second time is the one that counts.
Rate how close you've come to genuinely wrecking your own life, out of ten. Number first.~Over six, tell the story. Under six, I get to ask why you're being generous with yourself.
Name someone you lost that was your fault.~Then I ask one follow-up and you answer properly. You picked what to tell me — you don't pick the follow-up.
Guess what I actually think about when I can't sleep.~Then, on three, we both say the real one at the same time.
Say the ugliest true thing about why you're here tonight. Then I say mine.~Whoever's was uglier decides whether we keep going or move on.
Name a thing you've forgiven yourself for.~Then I rule on whether you'd earned it. If I say no, argue your case — and if you can't, sit with that.
Guess who in my life would be quietly relieved if I vanished for a year.~Then name yours. Neither of us gets to say 'nobody'.
Tell me the worst advice you gave that someone actually took. Then defend it as though it were good advice.~I decide whether you've convinced me. You probably haven't.

3.name: Too Far
q: What have you been thinking for the last ten minutes and not saying?~Say it exactly. Not the cleaned-up version.
On three, both say whether you want this to go anywhere.~Whatever comes out, you both live with it.
Name the thing about me you'd change if you could.~I'm not allowed to respond for thirty seconds. Then I tell you whether you're right.
Say the boldest thing you could say to me right now. It has to carry actual risk.~Then I rate the risk out of ten. Under five and you go again.
What am I doing tonight that's working on you?~Name the exact moment.
Guess which parts of tonight I've been performing. Name at least two.~Then I confirm or deny each one — and then I go after yours.
What would you regret not saying to me before this ends?~So say it now instead.
Guess what I'm hoping happens next. I'll tell you if you're right.
What's the question you've wanted to ask me all night?~Ask it. Out loud. Now.
Where does this actually go? Both answer at once — no hedging, no 'we'll see'.
Say the thing you'd only say if you knew you'd never see me again.~Say it as though that's true. Then deal with the fact that it isn't.
Guess what I decided about you in the first minute that I still think is true.~Then I tell you. Unedited version, and you asked for it.
Am I what you were hoping for?~The honest answer costs something. Pay it.
On three, both say what you're scared this turns into.~Same words or different — either way, you talk about the gap.
The truth about how much you like me. A number's allowed, but only if you explain it.~On three. No adjusting after you hear mine.
Say what you want to do right now that you're not going to do.~Then I say whether I'd have let you. Neither of us acts on it. That's the point.
Five seconds: what would you tell me if you were braver? Go.~Now say it properly, with the time you didn't have.
What's the story you'll tell about tonight?~Tell it now, to my face.
Name what I've got wrong about you tonight that you let slide. All of it.~I don't get to defend myself until you've finished.
If this is it — if we never do this again — what do you want me to know?~Both answer, on three. Whatever comes out, it stands.
Say the thing you're most afraid I'll agree with.~Then I tell you whether I do. No softening it.
Say what you want from me that you haven't asked for. Ask for it properly this time.~I have to give a real answer. Yes, no, or not yet. 'Maybe' isn't allowed.
Which of us is more into this? Both point on three.~Then talk about the answer.
What's the least honest thing you've said to me tonight?~Correct it now.
On three, both say the most honest thing you can about how you feel right this second.~Then stop talking for ten seconds. Both of you.
Guess the one thing I'll still be thinking about tomorrow.~Then I tell you, and you don't get to pretend you didn't hear it.
Rate, one to ten, how much you've held back tonight. Say your number before I say mine.~Whoever held back more goes first on the last card.
Name the moment tonight you nearly stopped being honest with me.~Then tell me what you said instead.
On three, both point at whoever has more to lose here.~Pointed at yourself? Say why out loud.
Say the thing you came here hoping you'd get to say.~If you already said it, say what you came hoping to hear instead.

wild: Hand over your phone. They read your last three sent messages out loud. No deleting first.
Swap phones. Sixty seconds, look wherever you want. Then they get the same.
They get to ask you one question — anything — and you answer it properly. Now.
Say the meanest true thing about me, then the kindest. In that order, no gap in between.
Hold eye contact until one of you says something real. Not until someone laughs — until someone says something real.
They pick something you're wearing or carrying. You give them the actual story, not the short version.
Do an impression of me. Be unkind about it. I'm not allowed to react.
Read out your last three searches. No scrolling past anything.
Say something you think will make them like you less. Then find out whether it did.
They rate you out of ten, out loud, and have to justify it.~You may not respond for thirty seconds.
Trade your worst secret of the night. They go first — you have to match it or beat it.
Whisper the thing you'd never say at normal volume. Then say it again, properly.
Both write down what you think happens after tonight. Show each other at the same time.
Say the last thing you'd want the other one to know about you. Out loud, no build-up.
final: Last card. Whatever you've been managing all night — the thing you kept just under the surface — stop managing it.
Say it plainly, once. Don't decorate it, and don't put a joke on the end.
Now you both know. Do something about it or don't — but you don't get to pretend it wasn't said.
